title: The Dance Begins
devanagari: चकार चण्डताण्डवं तनोतु नः शिवः शिवम्॥
translation: His neck is made holy by the streams of water flowing from the forest of his matted locks. On it hangs a long garland of mighty serpents. His damaru sounds damad damad damad damad, and Shiva dances the fierce Tandava. May that Shiva spread auspiciousness upon us.
translation_hi: जिनकी जटा रूपी वन से बहती जलधारा से पवित्र हुए कंठ में सर्पों की लंबी माला लटक रही है, और जिनका डमरू डमड् डमड् डमड् डमड् की ध्वनि कर रहा है, उन शिव ने प्रचंड तांडव किया। वे शिव हमारा कल्याण करें।

words.note: jata (matted hair) + atavi (forest). A + अ → आ.
Present participle of √gal. Before ज it becomes गलज्.
pavita = purified (causative of √pu); sthala = place. Locative.
Gerund of ava + √lamb. With a prefix the gerund ends in -य, not -त्वा.
Onomatopoeia: the words sound like what they mean.
damaru + ayam: उ before अ becomes व्.
Perfect tense of √kri (to do), used for story-past.
Neuter accusative: the thing he spreads.

grammar: Wordplay: शिवः शिवम्. The same word is the god's name (masculine, subject) and 'auspiciousness' (neuter, object): 'May Shiva spread shivam.'
Gerund with a prefix: अव + लम्ब् → अवलम्ब्य 'having hung'. Without a prefix you get -त्वा (दृष्ट्वा); with a prefix, -य.
Avagraha: गले + अवलम्ब्य → गलेऽवलम्ब्य, the same rule as कान्तेऽलि in the bee verse.
Perfect tense: चकार 'he did' is the tense of stories and epics, for events the speaker did not witness.
